sketches.mechanism: Optional chaining returns nil and silently stops evaluation when any link in the chain is nil
sketches.resonance: Reaching for someone through a chain of connections, but if any single link is absent, the whole reaching yields nothing — silently, without complaint.

sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, enforced by the compiler
sketches.resonance: Loneliness expressed as a language constraint: the type system guarantees there will never be another.

sketches.mechanism: In Elixir, variables are rebound (not mutated); the old binding is permanently shadowed and unreachable
sketches.resonance: Each time you become someone new, the person you were still exists somewhere underneath — but no expression can ever reach them again.
sketches.draft:
self = :child
self = :student
self = :lover
self = :stranger
# :child, :student, :lover — all still allocated, none recoverable
